links.evidence: Mar 17, 2026 special meeting, Item 1, 0:43:37 (City Manager, answering Councilmember O'Keefe's question at 0:43:06 on how each measure could address the structural deficit): the structural deficit is "somewhere in the neighborhood of $27 to $30 million"; were the sales tax to pass, "we would be able to mitigate some of the reductions to, our public safety" units.
links.label: Sales tax would mitigate cuts

links.evidence: Mar 17, 2026 special meeting, Item 1, 0:44:27 (City Manager; the Deputy City Manager refers to him at 0:45:36): the bond is "not so much focused on, like, a budget reduction, although … part of our budget deficit challenge in public works includes shifting a lot of people off of general fund and into special funds … if we add more special fund dollars through this measure … we would be able to, you know, offset some of those staff challenges."
links.label: Bond would move staff costs to special funds

links.evidence: Apr 28, 2026 regular meeting, 0:46:51 (Mayor Ishii, opening the consent calendar right after the Auditor's Financial Condition presentation): "our audit from our auditor really highlighted something that's important … we are facing a structural deficit of $30 million for FY27 and FY28," then asks members to bring budget referrals by May 19.
links.label: Mayor ties the audit to the budget

links.evidence: May 19, 2026 special meeting, Item 1, recorded action (annotated agenda): prepare ballot language for the 0.5% sales tax "to address the City's projected General Fund structural deficit and support essential City services"; the $300M GO bond "to fund priority infrastructure investments."
links.label: Sales tax adopted as deficit response

links.evidence: Mar 10, 2026: the City Auditor's report "City Contracts: Outdated Process Led to Non-Competitive Contracts" (Item 6), about 28 minutes with Council comment and public comment. Oct 27, 2026: Item 25, BMC 7.18 amendment requiring competitive procurement for services over $100,000 (Kesarwani; reviewed by the Budget & Finance Committee), first reading adopted on the consent calendar with no Council discussion; the City Auditor spoke for it in her comment slot (about 4 minutes).
links.label: Contracts audit → procurement ordinance, on consent
